items.desc: The agency aims to reduce testing costs, strengthen quality assurance and help Nepali products gain international recognition, but exporters say it could take up to three years to secure global accreditation.

items.desc: Kushal Bhurtel hits 99 off 51 balls as Pokhara Avengers pile up 224 for three against Kathmandu Gorkhas, the highest total in the competition’s history.

items.title: Changing farming practices threaten food and habitats of migratory birds
items.desc: The expansion of winter crops, shrinking wetlands, and rising use of pesticide are putting the survival of thousands of birds arriving in Nepal from Tibet, Mongolia, and Siberia at risk.

items.title: India approves weekly train service linking Janakpur and Ayodhya
items.desc: The 604-km cross-border service will connect two major Ramayana pilgrimage destinations, with stops in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh. The launch date and fares are yet to be announced.

items.title: Karnali sign off with consolation win as Chitwan finish fourth
items.desc: The Rhinos, already through to the playoffs, end the league stage on seven points after falling 24 runs short of a 154-run target.

items.title: Tinkar villagers face seven-hour walk for medical care
items.desc: With no health post in the border village, residents must take the sick across the border into India or walk seven hours to the nearest health facility. A community health centre built four years ago remains unused.

items.title: Bhattarai urges Prime Minister Shah to put five issues on agenda for India visit
items.desc: In an interview with Kantipur, the former prime minister says Nepal should press India on the border dispute, trade deficit, air routes and hydropower, while seeking trilateral cooperation on the Himalayan climate crisis.

items.title: Hydropower firms to need 50 percent construction progress for IPOs
items.desc: The proposed ordinance would allow companies to issue shares before commercial production begins, provided their projects have completed at least half of the physical work.

items.title: Karnali set Chitwan a target of 154 in final league match
items.desc: Hasan Talat hits an unbeaten half-century as Karnali Yakss, already out of playoff contention, post 153-8; Chitwan have secured a playoff berth.

items.title: Dhaulagiri Hospital still waiting for trauma centre a decade after announcement
items.desc: The Hari Khadka Trauma Centre, announced in 2015, remains short of buildings, staff and infrastructure despite the availability of equipment and some specialist doctors.

items.title: US air travel disruptions to persist until late on Sunday, FAA head says
items.desc: Federal Aviation Administration head Bryan Bedford said on Saturday that he expected airline operations to largely ​return to normal by late Sunday.

items.title: Bahrain issues first threat alerts since September as Iran says it attacked US base
items.desc: The Revolutionary Guards said they had launched ​six drones targeting a US air-defence radar at the Al-Rifaa helicopter ⁠base in Bahrain.

items.title: India’s Nitin Gadkari to attend Nepal Infrastructure Summit as keynote speaker
items.desc: The December 9–10 summit will bring together policymakers, investors and development partners to discuss infrastructure financing, regional connectivity and climate-resilient projects.

items.title: Jayanti Memorial Trust marks 25 years of expanding access to heart care
items.desc: Trust has supported more than 10,000 heart surgeries, organised cardiac health camps in 53 districts and provided heart health education to over 6,000 students.

items.title: Oil Corporation brings Rs300 billion in annual transactions under digital system
items.desc: More than 1,500 dealers, 60 bottlers and 60 airlines will be able to place fuel orders and make payments online through the new ERP system.

items.title: UK’s Prince William to be joined by wife Kate for visit to India
items.desc: Heir-to-the-throne William, 44, and Kate are flying out for a series of events across Mumbai during a three-day visit that includes Tuesday’s awards ceremony.

items.title: Nākaloka makes Kathmandu debut with an evening of music, devotion and silence
items.desc: The movement brought together spiritual traditions, music and meditative practices in an evening of collective reflection at Basantapur.

items.title: How Ishuta Shrestha found her calling in the fierce imagery of Paubha
items.desc: What began as a discovery in her grandfather’s room became her entry into Paubha and an exploration of faith, discipline and the symbolism of wrathful deities.

items.title: And then there were four: Lumbini lead NPL playoff pack
items.desc: The defending champions sealed the top spot with a four-wicket win over Biratnagar, leaving Sudurpaschim, Kathmandu and Chitwan to fight over second to fourth on Sunday.

items.title: SIPs attracted investors in the past. Current low returns frustrate them

items.title: Lamichhane asks China-bound MPs to keep third countries out of talks
items.desc: The RSP chair asks the 20-member delegation to focus on Nepal-China ties and study China’s experience in governance, technology and development.

items.title: Balendra Shah administration goes fast with ordinances: 13 issued, 2 forwarded in 8 months
items.desc: The Shah administration has issued 13 ordinances and recommended two more in less than eight months, despite commanding a near two-thirds majority in the House of Representatives.

items.title: Who is the real prime minister?
items.desc: After the IGP removal and journalist detentions, Lamichhane’s claim of a right to intervene has reopened a question the RSP’s landslide was meant to settle.

items.title: Congress leader Umesh Shrestha’s brother arrested in Inam Sapkota investigation
items.desc: Police say Mahesh Shrestha was arrested in Kirtipur after investigators found links between him and Sapkota, who is being investigated for alleged money laundering and banking offences.

items.title: Lumbini beat Biratnagar to reach Qualifier, Kings knocked out
items.desc: Ruben Trumpelmann seals a four-wicket victory with a six as the defending champions finish top of the league stage, while all four playoff spots are now decided.

items.title: Is Nepali politics forgetting its own history?
items.desc: From BP Koirala’s social democracy to the Maoists’ revolution, parties have experimented with big ideas in a short time. Few seem to look back at how those experiments went.
